title: Bad news: your AI application isn't that special
excerpt: Application startups are vulnerable to coming consolidation
content_html:
There are more than 70,000 AI companies operating today.

Most of them will not exist in five years.

Before you can see why — or figure out whether yours is one of them — you need a distinction the market keeps blurring.

Strip away the pitch decks and there are really only two types of AI system being built today.

CEO and founder of McMillanAI.

The first is AI infrastructure: the orchestration and governance technology that makes AI usable at scale. In plain terms, this is the plumbing — agent frameworks, model routing, evaluation and monitoring tools, guardrails, and the controls that let a large organization use AI safely.

It sits between the foundation models and the end user, and it is where an enormous amount of venture money is going right now.

The second is the surface application: the tool an actual person uses to do actual work. The underwriting assistant, the contract reviewer, the sales copilot. The thing with a login screen and a job to do.

What I see in the market is a blending of the two. Some firms are selling architecture.

Some are selling tools. Many are trying to sell both, on the theory that owning the whole stack is the safest position.

And while this market is filled with tremendous exuberance with seemingly everyone starting an AI company, I am very skeptical that many of these firms will ever see profitability as history offers a strong counter.

We've run this experiment twice.

The past and the future

The dot-com era ran the first version of this experiment, and its final tally is worth stating plainly. Researchers estimate that roughly 50,000 startups were founded in the United States between 1998 and 2002 to commercialize the internet.

Of those, something like 8,000 attracted venture funding. About 1,700 internet-related companies made it to an IPO across the whole era — 585 in 1999 and 2000 alone — and at the peak, only about 14 percent of the tech companies going public were profitable.

By late 2002, most internet stocks had lost more than three-quarters of their value and roughly 1.7 trillion dollars had been wiped out. And the number of enduring, large-scale winners from that entire cohort — Amazon, eBay, Priceline, Expedia — you can count on two hands. Run the funnel: 50,000 founded, 8,000 funded, 1,700 public, fewer than ten giants.

A real gold rush works the same way: a few strike it rich, some make a living, and most go home with less than they brought. This is important to remember for everything that follows.

If that funnel looks like a quirk of one bubble, it is not — it is how markets distribute winnings everywhere. Hendrik Bessembinder at Arizona State studied every U.S. stock since 1926, more than 25,000 companies, and found that the best-performing 4 percent account for all of the net wealth the stock market has ever created; the other 96 percent, taken together, did no better than Treasury bills.

Just 90 companies — a third of one percent — produced more than half of it, and the majority of stocks lost money outright over their lifetimes. The market wins; almost no individual company does. Keep that in mind every time someone tells you AI will create trillions in value. It will. That says nothing about whether any particular company captures a dime of it.

The example of cloud

Cloud computing is the sharper rerun. In the early days there were hundreds of cloud providers and a thriving ecosystem of middleware companies selling the connective tissue — provisioning tools, management layers, monitoring platforms.

Today three companies control roughly two-thirds of the cloud market, and their share grows every year.

And here is the part that matters for AI: the middleware layer did not consolidate alongside the platforms. It was absorbed by them. The hyperscalers built the management consoles, the monitoring, the orchestration, and shipped it as a feature. The companies whose entire business was cloud plumbing were acquired cheap or squeezed out.

Meanwhile, the application layer on top of that consolidated infrastructure exploded. Thousands of SaaS companies built durable, profitable businesses without owning a single server. The bottom of the stack ended up in a few hands. The top produced thousands of winners.

It has already happened once inside this stack

If cloud feels like ancient history, look at the data layer — the foundation every AI system sits on. That consolidation already occurred, and it finished recently. The "modern data stack" boom of the last decade funded hundreds of startups selling pipelines, catalogs, transformation tools, and warehouses.

Today the independent tier has settled to exactly two companies at scale: Snowflake and Databricks, each running at roughly five billion dollars in annual revenue, with the hyperscalers’ native offerings holding most of the rest of the market. Nearly everyone else was acquired, absorbed as a platform feature, or left scraping for the remainder.

And notice the shape it settled into. The top five data platforms — Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, and Microsoft’s offering — hold roughly two-thirds of the market. That is almost exactly where cloud landed: three players, about two-thirds of the market, a long tail fighting over the rest.

Two different layers, a decade apart, ending in the same proportions. That is not a coincidence. It is what happens when competing takes huge capital and the platforms can build whatever sits next to them. Expect the AI orchestration layer to end up the same way.

The consolidation was driven as much by the buyer as by the vendors. Large enterprises learned that scattered data is expensive data: every additional platform meant another copy of the truth, another integration, another security review, another contract.

So CTOs stopped buying data tools one team at a time and started making strategic platform decisions — pick one or two providers, consolidate the estate onto them, and hold that line. A single source of truth became an explicit architectural goal at most large companies, and once thousands of enterprises were making that same decision, the market had no room left for a long tail of vendors.

Look at what it took for Snowflake and Databricks to survive that consolidation: enormous capital, the fact that customers’ data lives on their platforms and is costly to move, and deep ties into how their customers work every day. You can survive as an independent alongside the hyperscalers — but only by becoming one of the few names a CTO puts on the strategic list, and almost nobody makes that list.

The same consolidation is coming for AI

Apply that pattern to the two types of AI company and the forecast writes itself.

The infrastructure layer — orchestration and governance — will consolidate down to a few. Not because the current tools are bad, but because this layer sits directly in the expansion path of the biggest players in technology. The model providers and hyperscalers have every incentive to build orchestration, evaluation, and governance into their platforms, and they are already doing it. Every capability that today justifies a standalone infrastructure startup is a roadmap item at a company with a hundred times the resources and a direct line to the same customers.

If you are building an architecture-only solution, this is the uncomfortable implication: you are likely to be taken out by one of the big players. Maybe you get acquired, if you are early and lucky. More often, the platform simply builds what you sell and includes it for free. Either way, orchestration and governance alone is not a business you can hold. The only real question is how long you have.

Which leaves the application layer as the open field. And this is the counterintuitive part: infrastructure consolidation is good news for application builders. When orchestration and governance become cheap, standardized, and built into the platforms, the cost of building a serious AI application collapses — just as commodity cloud ignited the SaaS boom. We are already seeing a massive increase in the number of AI applications getting built, and most will likely not survive.

Better software, worse odds

Part of what makes this cycle different is how little it costs to enter. Building serious software used to take millions in capital and a room full of engineers — a filter that limited how many companies could even try. Today a handful of people with AI tools can ship in weeks what took a funded startup a year.

So new ventures are multiplying, not because there are more good ideas, but because the cost of trying has collapsed. The scale tells the story: more than 70,000 AI companies operate globally today, roughly 18,000 to 30,000 of them in the United States alone.

The comparison to the dot-com era’s 50,000 is not perfectly apples to apples — that was a five-year founding total for one country, this is a snapshot of companies operating worldwide right now — but the order of magnitude is the same, this wave is global, and the count is still climbing.

Here is the twist that makes the coming shakeout more brutal, not less: the software being built is genuinely good. This is not the dot-com era, where half-finished products hid behind splashy marketing. The tools are now so powerful that quality is the baseline — which means quality has stopped differentiating anything. When every product is polished, capable, and shipped fast, none of that separates you from the next founder who did the same thing last month.

And that is precisely why so few founders see the danger. Every one of them genuinely believes they are building something singular — and by their own measure, they are right. They compare their product to what came before: the clunky incumbent, the manual process, the way the work used to get done. Against that benchmark it looks revolutionary.

What they never compare it to is the tens of thousands of other teams looking at the same models and the same problems, building virtually the same thing at the same time. Measured against the past, every AI product is remarkable. Measured against the field, almost none are. More entrants than either previous cycle, all building excellent software, almost none of it distinguishable.

That is the setup for the largest culling yet, and it will run almost entirely on the moats, because there is nothing else left to separate the winners from the losers.

The delusion of special

I see this up close. I have this conversation with application founders every week, and it always goes the same way. They believe the quality of what they built is their moat: the product works, customers love it, nothing else on the market feels as good.

All of that can be true, and none of it protects them. Quality can be copied. The same tools that let them build an excellent product in months let a competitor build one in weeks. A few founders have built something that truly stands alone, but I just can’t see many finding a way to real profitability.

There will be some winners, but I think they will need to rest on three key differentiators:

1. Data. Not data you scraped or licensed — proprietary data your business generates by operating: claims histories, transaction flows, patient outcomes. If your system gets smarter from data competitors cannot obtain at any price, you compound. If you are building on the same public internet as everyone else, you do not.

2. Distribution. If you already own the customer relationship — an installed base, a trusted brand, an embedded sales channel — you can put an AI product in front of buyers faster and cheaper than any startup. This is why incumbents are more dangerous in this cycle than the last one. The startup has to build the product and buy the audience. The incumbent only has to build the product.

3. Integration into workflows. The one people underestimate. Companies that wire themselves into how work actually gets done — the approvals, the systems of record, the daily habits of thousands of employees — become painful to remove even when a rival ships something better. Switching costs are not glamorous, but they have protected enterprise software for thirty years, and they will protect AI applications too.

Have one of these and you can build a durable business on commodity infrastructure. Have two and you can build a great one. Have none and you are likely running out of time.

Your toughest competitor is your customer

And here is what makes the application layer even harder than the dot-com or SaaS eras: surface applications are not just competing with other vendors. They are competing with the companies they are trying to sell to. The same commodity infrastructure that makes it easy for a startup to spin up an AI application makes it just as easy for the buyer to build one internally.

Every enterprise pitch now runs into a question that barely existed in the SaaS era: why would we buy this when a small internal team could build it in a quarter?

And here is the uncomfortable part. The three advantages that decide the application winners — distribution, proprietary data, embedded workflows — are precisely what the buyer already has. The enterprise owns its data. It is its own distribution. It controls its own workflows. The customer starts the build-versus-buy conversation holding every moat you are trying to claim.

A surface application does not just need to be better than its competitors. It needs to be so much better than what the customer could build themselves that buying beats owning — and that bar rises every time the underlying infrastructure gets easier to use.

Know which company you are

I am not going to pretend to know which specific firms win. But the structure of the outcome is already visible, because we have now watched it three times — dot-com, cloud, and the data layer: infrastructure consolidates to a few, applications proliferate, and the survivors are the ones holding data, distribution, or workflow integration that cannot be copied.

So the first question is not "is my product good?" It is "which of the two companies am I?" If you are infrastructure, your realistic endgame is being bought or being bypassed — plan accordingly. If you are an application, the model is not your moat and the product probably is not either.

So what is?

The good news, and who gets it

One clarification before closing, because everything above can read as pessimism about AI itself. It is the opposite. The technology will create enormous value, and the markets built on it will grow. The open question is who keeps that value, and a century of evidence gives a consistent answer: mostly the consumers of a technology, not its producers.

William Nordhaus at Yale measured this across decades of American innovation and found that producers capture only about 2 percent of the total value their innovations create — the rest flows to the people and businesses that use them. Railroads transformed the economy and ruined most of their investors. Airlines moved the world and destroyed capital for a hundred years. The internet made a handful of platforms rich — and made every company that deployed it more productive.

This cycle is already tracing the same shape: the infrastructure layer consolidates, prices its scarcity, and books historic profits, while the application layer competes and hands its margin to the buyer.

That is the real ending of this story. The coming massacre of AI companies and the coming growth of the AI economy are the same event, seen from opposite sides of the table. If you sell AI, the funnel is your problem and the moats are your only defense.

If you buy AI, the competition among 70,000 firms is working precisely in your favor: every improvement, every price cut, every copied feature moves value from their side of the table to yours. The bad news in this article is only bad depending on which chair you sit in.

blocks.html_en: The example of cloud

sentences.en: The example of cloud
sentences.zh: 云的例子

blocks.html_en: Cloud computing is the sharper rerun. In the early days there were hundreds of cloud providers and a thriving ecosystem of middleware companies selling the connective tissue — provisioning tools, management layers, monitoring platforms.

sentences.en: Cloud computing is the sharper rerun.
sentences.zh: 云计算是更尖锐的重演。

sentences.en: In the early days there were hundreds of cloud providers and a thriving ecosystem of middleware companies selling the connective tissue — provisioning tools, management layers, monitoring platforms.
sentences.zh: 早期有数百家云提供商和一个由销售结缔组织（配置工具、管理层、监控平台）的中间件公司组成的蓬勃发展的生态系统。

blocks.html_en: Today three companies control roughly two-thirds of the cloud market, and their share grows every year.

sentences.en: Today three companies control roughly two-thirds of the cloud market, and their share grows every year.
sentences.zh: 如今，三家公司控制着大约三分之二的云市场，而且它们的份额每年都在增长。

blocks.html_en: And here is the part that matters for AI: the middleware layer did not consolidate alongside the platforms. It was absorbed by them. The hyperscalers built the management consoles, the monitoring, the orchestration, and shipped it as a feature. The companies whose entire business was cloud plumbing were acquired cheap or squeezed out.

sentences.en: And here is the part that matters for AI: the middleware layer did not consolidate alongside the platforms.
sentences.zh: 对于人工智能来说，最重要的部分是：中间件层没有与平台一起整合。

sentences.en: It was absorbed by them.
sentences.zh: 被他们吸收了。

sentences.en: The hyperscalers built the management consoles, the monitoring, the orchestration, and shipped it as a feature.
sentences.zh: 超大规模企业构建了管理控制台、监控、编排，并将其作为一项功能提供。

sentences.en: The companies whose entire business was cloud plumbing were acquired cheap or squeezed out.
sentences.zh: 整个业务都是云管道的公司要么被廉价收购，要么被挤出。

blocks.html_en: Meanwhile, the application layer on top of that consolidated infrastructure exploded. Thousands of SaaS companies built durable, profitable businesses without owning a single server. The bottom of the stack ended up in a few hands. The top produced thousands of winners.

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the application layer on top of that consolidated infrastructure exploded.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，整合基础设施之上的应用层发生了爆炸性的增长。

sentences.en: Thousands of SaaS companies built durable, profitable businesses without owning a single server.
sentences.zh: 数以千计的 SaaS 公司在没有拥有一台服务器的情况下建立了持久、盈利的业务。

sentences.en: The bottom of the stack ended up in a few hands.
sentences.zh: 筹码堆的底部最终落在了几手牌上。

sentences.en: The top produced thousands of winners.
sentences.zh: 顶端产生了数千名获胜者。

blocks.html_en: It has already happened once inside this stack

sentences.en: It has already happened once inside this stack
sentences.zh: 它已经在这个堆栈中发生过一次

blocks.html_en: If cloud feels like ancient history, look at the data layer — the foundation every AI system sits on. That consolidation already occurred, and it finished recently. The "modern data stack" boom of the last decade funded hundreds of startups selling pipelines, catalogs, transformation tools, and warehouses.

sentences.en: If cloud feels like ancient history, look at the data layer — the foundation every AI system sits on.
sentences.zh: 如果云感觉像是古老的历史，那么看看数据层——每个人工智能系统的基础。

sentences.en: That consolidation already occurred, and it finished recently.
sentences.zh: 这种整合已经发生，并且最近才结束。

sentences.en: The "modern data stack" boom of the last decade funded hundreds of startups selling pipelines, catalogs, transformation tools, and warehouses.
sentences.zh: 过去十年的“现代数据堆栈”繁荣资助了数百家销售管道、目录、转换工具和仓库的初创公司。

blocks.html_en: Today the independent tier has settled to exactly two companies at scale: Snowflake and Databricks, each running at roughly five billion dollars in annual revenue, with the hyperscalers’ native offerings holding most of the rest of the market. Nearly everyone else was acquired, absorbed as a platform feature, or left scraping for the remainder.

sentences.en: Today the independent tier has settled to exactly two companies at scale: Snowflake and Databricks, each running at roughly five billion dollars in annual revenue, with the hyperscalers’ native offerings holding most of the rest of the market.
sentences.zh: 如今，独立层已经形成规模化的两家公司：Snowflake 和 Databricks，每家公司的年收入约为 50 亿美元，而超大规模企业的本地产品占据了大部分市场份额。

sentences.en: Nearly everyone else was acquired, absorbed as a platform feature, or left scraping for the remainder.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有其他人都被收购了，被吸收为平台功能，或者留下了剩下的东西。

blocks.html_en: And notice the shape it settled into. The top five data platforms — Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, and Microsoft’s offering — hold roughly two-thirds of the market. That is almost exactly where cloud landed: three players, about two-thirds of the market, a long tail fighting over the rest.

sentences.en: And notice the shape it settled into.
sentences.zh: 并注意它所形成的形状。

sentences.en: The top five data platforms — Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, and Microsoft’s offering — hold roughly two-thirds of the market.
sentences.zh: 排名前五的数据平台——Snowflake、BigQuery、Redshift、Databricks 和微软的产品——占据了大约三分之二的市场份额。

sentences.en: That is almost exactly where cloud landed: three players, about two-thirds of the market, a long tail fighting over the rest.
sentences.zh: 这几乎正​​是云落地的地方：三个参与者，大约三分之二的市场，长尾争夺其余市场。

blocks.html_en: Two different layers, a decade apart, ending in the same proportions. That is not a coincidence. It is what happens when competing takes huge capital and the platforms can build whatever sits next to them. Expect the AI orchestration layer to end up the same way.

sentences.en: Two different layers, a decade apart, ending in the same proportions.
sentences.zh: 两个不同的层，相隔十年，以相同的比例结束。

sentences.en: That is not a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 这并非巧合。

sentences.en: It is what happens when competing takes huge capital and the platforms can build whatever sits next to them.
sentences.zh: 当竞争需要巨额资本并且平台可以建造任何毗邻的东西时，就会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Expect the AI orchestration layer to end up the same way.
sentences.zh: 预计人工智能编排层也会以同样的方式结束。

blocks.html_en: The consolidation was driven as much by the buyer as by the vendors. Large enterprises learned that scattered data is expensive data: every additional platform meant another copy of the truth, another integration, another security review, another contract.

sentences.en: The consolidation was driven as much by the buyer as by the vendors.
sentences.zh: 买家和卖家都推动了整合。

sentences.en: Large enterprises learned that scattered data is expensive data: every additional platform meant another copy of the truth, another integration, another security review, another contract.
sentences.zh: 大型企业了解到，分散的数据是昂贵的数据：每个额外的平台都意味着另一个事实副本、另一个集成、另一个安全审查、另一个合同。

blocks.html_en: So CTOs stopped buying data tools one team at a time and started making strategic platform decisions — pick one or two providers, consolidate the estate onto them, and hold that line. A single source of truth became an explicit architectural goal at most large companies, and once thousands of enterprises were making that same decision, the market had no room left for a long tail of vendors.

sentences.en: So CTOs stopped buying data tools one team at a time and started making strategic platform decisions — pick one or two providers, consolidate the estate onto them, and hold that line.
sentences.zh: 因此，首席技术官不再一次为一个团队购买数据工具，而是开始制定战略平台决策——选择一两个提供商，将资产整合到他们身上，并坚持下去。

sentences.en: A single source of truth became an explicit architectural goal at most large companies, and once thousands of enterprises were making that same decision, the market had no room left for a long tail of vendors.
sentences.zh: 单一事实来源成为大多数大公司的明确架构目标，一旦成千上万的企业做出同样的决定，市场就没有空间容纳长尾供应商。

blocks.html_en: Look at what it took for Snowflake and Databricks to survive that consolidation: enormous capital, the fact that customers’ data lives on their platforms and is costly to move, and deep ties into how their customers work every day. You can survive as an independent alongside the hyperscalers — but only by becoming one of the few names a CTO puts on the strategic list, and almost nobody makes that list.

sentences.en: Look at what it took for Snowflake and Databricks to survive that consolidation: enormous capital, the fact that customers’ data lives on their platforms and is costly to move, and deep ties into how their customers work every day.
sentences.zh: 看看 Snowflake 和 Databricks 是如何在这场整合中幸存下来的：巨大的资本、客户的数据存储在他们的平台上且移动成本高昂的事实，以及与客户日常工作方式的紧密联系。

sentences.en: You can survive as an independent alongside the hyperscalers — but only by becoming one of the few names a CTO puts on the strategic list, and almost nobody makes that list.
sentences.zh: 你可以作为独立企业与超大规模企业一起生存——但前提是成为 CTO 列入战略名单的少数几个名字之一，而几乎没有人上榜。

blocks.html_en: The same consolidation is coming for AI

sentences.en: The same consolidation is coming for AI
sentences.zh: 人工智能也将面临同样的整合

blocks.html_en: Apply that pattern to the two types of AI company and the forecast writes itself.

sentences.en: Apply that pattern to the two types of AI company and the forecast writes itself.
sentences.zh: 将这种模式应用到两种类型的人工智能公司上，预测就会自动生成。

blocks.html_en: The infrastructure layer — orchestration and governance — will consolidate down to a few. Not because the current tools are bad, but because this layer sits directly in the expansion path of the biggest players in technology. The model providers and hyperscalers have every incentive to build orchestration, evaluation, and governance into their platforms, and they are already doing it. Every capability that today justifies a standalone infrastructure startup is a roadmap item at a company with a hundred times the resources and a direct line to the same customers.

sentences.en: The infrastructure layer — orchestration and governance — will consolidate down to a few.
sentences.zh: 基础设施层——编排和治理——将整合到几个层。

sentences.en: Not because the current tools are bad, but because this layer sits directly in the expansion path of the biggest players in technology.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为当前的工具很糟糕，而是因为这一层直接位于技术领域最大参与者的扩张路径中。

sentences.en: The model providers and hyperscalers have every incentive to build orchestration, evaluation, and governance into their platforms, and they are already doing it.
sentences.zh: 模型提供商和超大规模提供商有充分的动力将编排、评估和治理构建到他们的平台中，而且他们已经在这样做了。

sentences.en: Every capability that today justifies a standalone infrastructure startup is a roadmap item at a company with a hundred times the resources and a direct line to the same customers.
sentences.zh: 如今，独立基础设施初创公司的每一项功能都是一个路线图项目，该公司拥有一百倍的资源，并且与相同的客户有直接联系。

blocks.html_en: If you are building an architecture-only solution, this is the uncomfortable implication: you are likely to be taken out by one of the big players. Maybe you get acquired, if you are early and lucky. More often, the platform simply builds what you sell and includes it for free. Either way, orchestration and governance alone is not a business you can hold. The only real question is how long you have.

sentences.en: If you are building an architecture-only solution, this is the uncomfortable implication: you are likely to be taken out by one of the big players.
sentences.zh: 如果您正在构建纯架构解决方案，这就是令人不安的含义：您可能会被其中一个大玩家淘汰。

sentences.en: Maybe you get acquired, if you are early and lucky.
sentences.zh: 如果你早且幸运的话，也许你会被收购。

sentences.en: More often, the platform simply builds what you sell and includes it for free.
sentences.zh: 更常见的是，该平台只是构建您销售的产品并免费包含它。

sentences.en: Either way, orchestration and governance alone is not a business you can hold.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，仅靠编排和治理都不是您可以持有的业务。

sentences.en: The only real question is how long you have.
sentences.zh: 唯一真正的问题是你还有多长时间。

blocks.html_en: Which leaves the application layer as the open field. And this is the counterintuitive part: infrastructure consolidation is good news for application builders. When orchestration and governance become cheap, standardized, and built into the platforms, the cost of building a serious AI application collapses — just as commodity cloud ignited the SaaS boom. We are already seeing a massive increase in the number of AI applications getting built, and most will likely not survive.

sentences.en: Which leaves the application layer as the open field.
sentences.zh: 这使得应用层成为开放领域。

sentences.en: And this is the counterintuitive part: infrastructure consolidation is good news for application builders.
sentences.zh: 这是违反直觉的部分：基础设施整合对于应用程序构建者来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: When orchestration and governance become cheap, standardized, and built into the platforms, the cost of building a serious AI application collapses — just as commodity cloud ignited the SaaS boom.
sentences.zh: 当编排和治理变得廉价、标准化并内置于平台中时，构建重要的人工智能应用程序的成本就会大幅下降——就像商品云引发了 SaaS 热潮一样。

sentences.en: We are already seeing a massive increase in the number of AI applications getting built, and most will likely not survive.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到人工智能应用程序的数量大幅增加，但大多数可能无法生存。

sentences.en: Better software, worse odds
sentences.zh: 更好的软件，更糟糕的胜算

blocks.html_en: Part of what makes this cycle different is how little it costs to enter. Building serious software used to take millions in capital and a room full of engineers — a filter that limited how many companies could even try. Today a handful of people with AI tools can ship in weeks what took a funded startup a year.

sentences.en: Part of what makes this cycle different is how little it costs to enter.
sentences.zh: 这个周期的不同之处在于其进入成本非常低。

sentences.en: Building serious software used to take millions in capital and a room full of engineers — a filter that limited how many companies could even try.
sentences.zh: 过去，构建严肃的软件需要数百万美元的资金和一屋子的工程师——这个过滤器限制了有多少公司可以尝试。

sentences.en: Today a handful of people with AI tools can ship in weeks what took a funded startup a year.
sentences.zh: 如今，少数拥有人工智能工具的人可以在几周内完成一家初创公司需要一年才能完成的任务。

blocks.html_en: So new ventures are multiplying, not because there are more good ideas, but because the cost of trying has collapsed. The scale tells the story: more than 70,000 AI companies operate globally today, roughly 18,000 to 30,000 of them in the United States alone.

sentences.en: So new ventures are multiplying, not because there are more good ideas, but because the cost of trying has collapsed.
sentences.zh: 因此，新的企业不断涌现，并不是因为有更多好的想法，而是因为尝试的成本已经大幅下降。

sentences.en: The scale tells the story: more than 70,000 AI companies operate globally today, roughly 18,000 to 30,000 of them in the United States alone.
sentences.zh: 规模说明了这一点：当今全球有超过 70,000 家人工智能公司在运营，其中仅美国就有大约 18,000 至 30,000 家。

blocks.html_en: The comparison to the dot-com era’s 50,000 is not perfectly apples to apples — that was a five-year founding total for one country, this is a snapshot of companies operating worldwide right now — but the order of magnitude is the same, this wave is global, and the count is still climbing.

sentences.en: The comparison to the dot-com era’s 50,000 is not perfectly apples to apples — that was a five-year founding total for one country, this is a snapshot of companies operating worldwide right now — but the order of magnitude is the same, this wave is global, and the count is still climbing.
sentences.zh: 与互联网时代的 50,000 家公司相比，并不完全是同类的——这是一个国家成立五年的总数，这是目前在全球范围内运营的公司的快照——但数量级是相同的，这一波浪潮是全球性的，而且数量仍在攀升。

blocks.html_en: Here is the twist that makes the coming shakeout more brutal, not less: the software being built is genuinely good. This is not the dot-com era, where half-finished products hid behind splashy marketing. The tools are now so powerful that quality is the baseline — which means quality has stopped differentiating anything. When every product is polished, capable, and shipped fast, none of that separates you from the next founder who did the same thing last month.

content_html_zh:
目前有超过 70,000 家人工智能公司在运营。

其中大多数在五年内将不复存在。

在你明白原因之前——或者弄清楚你的产品是否属于其中之一——你需要区分市场不断模糊的情况。

抛开融资演讲稿，目前正在构建的人工智能系统实际上只有两种类型。

McMillanAI 的首席执行官兼创始人。

第一个是人工智能基础设施：使人工智能大规模可用的编排和治理技术。 简单来说，这就是管道——代理框架、模型路由、评估和监控工具、护栏以及让大型组织安全使用人工智能的控制措施。

它位于基础模型和最终用户之间，也是目前大量风险投资的去向。

第二个是表面应用：实际的人用来做实际工作的工具。 承保助理、合同审核员、销售副驾驶。 带有登录屏幕和要做的工作的东西。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

我在市场上看到的是两者的混合。 一些公司正在销售建筑。

有些是卖工具的。 许多人试图出售两者，因为理论上拥有整个堆栈是最安全的位置。

尽管这个市场充满了巨大的繁荣，似乎每个人都创办了一家人工智能公司，但我非常怀疑这些公司中的许多公司能否实现盈利，因为历史提供了强有力的反驳。

我们已经进行了两次这个实验。

过去与未来

互联网时代进行了这个实验的第一个版本，其最终结果值得明确说明。 研究人员估计，1998 年至 2002 年间，美国大约成立了 50,000 家初创公司，将互联网商业化。

其中，约有 8,000 家吸引了风险投资。 整个时代大约有 1,700 家互联网相关公司进行了 IPO（仅 1999 年和 2000 年就有 585 家），而在高峰时期，只有约 14% 的上市科技公司实现了盈利。

到 2002 年底，大多数互联网股票的价值已经损失了四分之三以上，大约 1.7 万亿美元被蒸发。 而亚马逊、eBay、Priceline、Expedia 等整个群体中持久的大规模赢家的数量，你两只手都可以数得出来。 运行漏斗：50,000 家创立，8,000 家资助，1,700 家公众，不到 10 个巨头。

真正的淘金热也是如此：一些人致富，一些人谋生，而大多数人带着比他们带来的更少的钱回家。 对于接下来的一切，记住这一点很重要。

如果这个漏斗看起来像是一个泡沫的怪癖，那么事实并非如此——这就是市场在各地分配利润的方式。 亚利桑那州立大学的亨德里克·贝塞宾德 (Hendrik Bessembinder) 研究了 1926 年以来的每支美国股票，超过 25,000 家公司，发现表现最好的 4% 占据了股市有史以来创造的全部净财富；剩下的 96% 加在一起，表现并不比国库券好。

只有 90 家公司（百分之一的三分之一）生产了一半以上的股票，而且大多数股票在其生命周期内都直接亏损。 市场获胜；几乎没有个别公司这样做。 每当有人告诉你人工智能将创造数万亿美元的价值时，请记住这一点。 会的。 这并没有说明是否有任何特定公司从中获得了一分钱。

云的例子

云计算是更尖锐的重演。 早期有数百家云提供商和一个由销售结缔组织（配置工具、管理层、监控平台）的中间件公司组成的蓬勃发展的生态系统。

如今，三家公司控制着大约三分之二的云市场，而且它们的份额每年都在增长。

对于人工智能来说，最重要的部分是：中间件层没有与平台一起整合。 被他们吸收了。 超大规模企业构建了管理控制台、监控、编排，并将其作为一项功能提供。 整个业务都是云管道的公司要么被廉价收购，要么被挤出。

与此同时，整合基础设施之上的应用层发生了爆炸性的增长。 数以千计的 SaaS 公司在没有拥有一台服务器的情况下建立了持久、盈利的业务。 筹码堆的底部最终落在了几手牌上。 顶端产生了数千名获胜者。

它已经在这个堆栈中发生过一次

如果云感觉像是古老的历史，那么看看数据层——每个人工智能系统的基础。 这种整合已经发生，并且最近才结束。 过去十年的“现代数据堆栈”繁荣资助了数百家销售管道、目录、转换工具和仓库的初创公司。

如今，独立层已经形成规模化的两家公司：Snowflake 和 Databricks，每家公司的年收入约为 50 亿美元，而超大规模企业的本地产品占据了大部分市场份额。 几乎所有其他人都被收购了，被吸收为平台功能，或者留下了剩下的东西。

并注意它所形成的形状。 排名前五的数据平台——Snowflake、BigQuery、Redshift、Databricks 和微软的产品——占据了大约三分之二的市场份额。 这几乎正​​是云落地的地方：三个参与者，大约三分之二的市场，长尾争夺其余市场。

两个不同的层，相隔十年，以相同的比例结束。 这并非巧合。 当竞争需要巨额资本并且平台可以建造任何毗邻的东西时，就会发生这种情况。 预计人工智能编排层也会以同样的方式结束。

买家和卖家都推动了整合。 大型企业了解到，分散的数据是昂贵的数据：每个额外的平台都意味着另一个事实副本、另一个集成、另一个安全审查、另一个合同。

因此，首席技术官不再一次为一个团队购买数据工具，而是开始制定战略平台决策——选择一两个提供商，将资产整合到他们身上，并坚持下去。 单一事实来源成为大多数大公司的明确架构目标，一旦成千上万的企业做出同样的决定，市场就没有空间容纳长尾供应商。

看看 Snowflake 和 Databricks 是如何在这场整合中幸存下来的：巨大的资本、客户的数据存储在他们的平台上且移动成本高昂的事实，以及与客户日常工作方式的紧密联系。 你可以作为独立企业与超大规模企业一起生存——但前提是成为 CTO 列入战略名单的少数几个名字之一，而几乎没有人上榜。

人工智能也将面临同样的整合

将这种模式应用到两种类型的人工智能公司上，预测就会自动生成。

基础设施层——编排和治理——将整合到几个层。 并不是因为当前的工具很糟糕，而是因为这一层直接位于技术领域最大参与者的扩张路径中。 模型提供商和超大规模提供商有充分的动力将编排、评估和治理构建到他们的平台中，而且他们已经在这样做了。 如今，独立基础设施初创公司的每一项功能都是一个路线图项目，该公司拥有一百倍的资源，并且与相同的客户有直接联系。

如果您正在构建纯架构解决方案，这就是令人不安的含义：您可能会被其中一个大玩家淘汰。 如果你早且幸运的话，也许你会被收购。 更常见的是，该平台只是构建您销售的产品并免费包含它。 无论哪种方式，仅靠编排和治理都不是您可以持有的业务。 唯一真正的问题是你还有多长时间。

这使得应用层成为开放领域。 这是违反直觉的部分：基础设施整合对于应用程序构建者来说是个好消息。 当编排和治理变得廉价、标准化并内置于平台中时，构建重要的人工智能应用程序的成本就会大幅下降——就像商品云引发了 SaaS 热潮一样。 我们已经看到人工智能应用程序的数量大幅增加，但大多数可能无法生存。

更好的软件，更糟糕的胜算

这个周期的不同之处在于其进入成本非常低。 过去，构建严肃的软件需要数百万美元的资金和一屋子的工程师——这个过滤器限制了有多少公司可以尝试。 如今，少数拥有人工智能工具的人可以在几周内完成一家初创公司需要一年才能完成的任务。

因此，新的企业不断涌现，并不是因为有更多好的想法，而是因为尝试的成本已经大幅下降。 规模说明了这一点：当今全球有超过 70,000 家人工智能公司在运营，其中仅美国就有大约 18,000 至 30,000 家。

与互联网时代的 50,000 家公司相比，并不完全是同类的——这是一个国家成立五年的总数，这是目前在全球范围内运营的公司的快照——但数量级是相同的，这一波浪潮是全球性的，而且数量仍在攀升。

这里有一个转折，使即将到来的洗牌变得更加残酷，而不是更少：正在构建的软件确实很好。 现在不是互联网时代，半成品隐藏在铺天盖地的营销背后。 现在的工具是如此强大，以至于质量成为了基准——这意味着质量已经不再让任何东西与众不同。 当每件产品都经过精心打磨、功能强大且发货速度快时，所有这些都无法将您与上个月做了同样事情的下一位创始人区分开来。

这正是为什么很少有创始人看到这种危险的原因。 他们每个人都真诚地相信自己正在构建一些独特的东西——并且以他们自己的衡量标准来看，他们是对的。 他们将自己的产品与以前的产品进行比较：笨重的现有产品、手动流程、过去完成工作的方式。 与这个基准相比，它看起来是革命性的。

他们从未将其与数以万计的其他团队进行比较，这些团队正在研究相同的模型和相同的问题，同时构建几乎相同的东西。 与过去相比，每一个人工智能产品都是非凡的。 与现场相比，几乎没有。 比之前的任何一个周期都有更多的进入者，他们都构建了优秀的软件，几乎没有一个是可以区分的。

这是迄今为止最大规模的扑杀行动，而且它将几乎完全在护城河上进行，因为没有任何其他东西可以区分赢家和输家。

特别的错觉

我近距离看到了这一点。 我每周都会与应用程序创始人进行这样的对话，而且总是以同样的方式进行。 他们相信他们所创造的产品的质量是他们的护城河：产品有效，客户喜欢它，市场上没有其他产品感觉如此好。

所有这些都可能是真的，但它们都不能保护他们。 品质是可以复制的。 同样的工具可以让他们在几个月内开发出一款优秀的产品，而竞争对手却可以在几周内开发出一款产品。 一些创始人已经建立了真正独立的东西，但我看不到很多创始人找到了真正盈利的方法。

将会有一些赢家，但我认为他们需要依靠三个关键的差异化优势：

1. 数据。 不是您抓取或许可的数据 - 您的企业通过操作生成的专有数据：索赔历史、交易流程、患者结果。 如果您的系统从竞争对手无法以任何价格获得的数据中变得更加智能，那么您就会复合。 如果您与其他人一样在同一个公共互联网上进行构建，那么您就不会这样做。

2. 分配。 如果你已经拥有了客户关系——一个已安装的基础、一个值得信赖的品牌、一个嵌入式销售渠道——你就可以比任何初创公司更快、更便宜地向买家展示人工智能产品。 这就是为什么现任者在这个周期中比上一个周期更危险。 初创公司必须打造产品并购买受众。 现任者只需构建产品。

3. 集成到工作流程中。 被人们低估的人。 即使竞争对手推出了更好的产品，那些将自己与工作实际完成方式（审批、记录系统、数千名员工的日常习惯）联系起来的公司也会变得痛苦。 转换成本并不光彩，但它们已经保护了企业软件三十年，它们也将保护人工智能应用程序。

拥有其中之一，您就可以在商品基础设施上建立持久的业务。 拥有两个，您就可以打造出一款出色的产品。 如果没有，您可能已经没有时间了。

你最强大的竞争对手是你的客户

这就是应用程序层比互联网或 SaaS 时代更加困难的原因：表面应用程序不仅仅是与其他供应商竞争。 他们正在与他们试图出售产品的公司竞争。 同样的商品基础设施可以让初创公司轻松启动人工智能应用程序，也让买家可以轻松地在内部构建人工智能应用程序。

现在每个企业推销都会遇到一个在 SaaS 时代几乎不存在的问题：当一个小型内部团队可以在一个季度内构建它时，我们为什么要购买它？

这是令人不舒服的部分。 决定应用程序获胜者的三个优势——分发、专有数据、嵌入式工作流程——正是买家已经拥有的。 企业拥有自己的数据。 它是它自己的发行版。 它控制自己的工作流程。 客户开始进行“构建与购买”对话，掌握着您试图夺取的每一条护城河。

表面应用不仅需要比竞争对手更好。 它需要比客户自己构建的东西要好得多，以至于购买胜过拥有——而且每当底层基础设施变得更容易使用时，这个门槛就会提高。

知道你是哪家公司

我不会假装知道哪些特定公司获胜。 但结果的结构已经可见，因为我们现在已经看过三遍了——互联网、云和数据层：基础设施整合到少数，应用程序激增，而幸存者是那些拥有无法复制的数据、分发或工作流程集成的人。

所以第一个问题不是“我的产品好不好？” 问题是“我是这两家公司中的哪一家？” 如果你是基础设施，你现实的结局是被购买或被绕过——相应地计划。 如果您是一个应用程序，那么模型不是您的护城河，产品也可能不是。

那么什么是？

好消息，以及谁得到它

结束前需要澄清一点，因为以上所有内容都可以解读为对人工智能本身的悲观主义。 事实恰恰相反。 该技术将创造巨大的价值，以其为基础的市场将会增长。 悬而未决的问题是谁保留了这种价值，一个世纪的证据给出了一致的答案：主要是技术的消费者，而不是其生产者。

耶鲁大学的威廉·诺德豪斯（William Nordhaus）对美国数十年的创新进行了衡量，发现生产者只获得了其创新创造的总价值的约 2%，其余的流向了使用它们的人和企业。 铁路改变了经济，也毁掉了大部分投资者。 一百年来，航空公司推动了世界并摧毁了首都。 互联网让少数平台变得更加丰富，也让每家部署它的公司变得更加高效。

这个周期已经呈现出相同的形状：基础设施层进行整合，对其稀缺性进行定价，并获得历史性利润，而应用程序层则进行竞争，并将其利润交给买家。

这才是这个故事真正的结局。 即将到来的人工智能公司屠杀和即将到来的人工智能经济增长是同一件事，从桌子的两端来看。 如果你卖人工智能，漏斗就是你的问题，护城河是你唯一的防御。

如果你购买人工智能，那么 70,000 家公司之间的竞争正是对你有利：每一次改进、每一次降价、每一次复制的功能都会将价值从他们的一方转移到你的一方。 本文中的坏消息是否坏取决于您坐在哪把椅子上。
